title: Head, tail, back, belly

objective.text: Name the three axes of the flat week-3 embryonic disc.

body.general: Which end of a flat disc is the head? Its head–tail and back–belly directions are fixed before gastrulation starts [f1]. Head to tail is the long axis: a groove forms at the tail end, so the head end is opposite it [f2,f3]. Back to belly runs through the disc: the upper layer faces the back, the lower layer faces the belly [f4]. Left and right are the embryo's own sides, not yours [f5].
body.mbbs: The disc has cranial–caudal and dorsal–ventral axes before the primitive streak appears [f1]. The cranial–caudal axis is the long axis: the streak forms in the caudal midline, and the cranial end lies opposite it [f2,f3]. The dorsal–ventral axis runs through the disc: dorsal is the upper side facing the amniotic cavity, ventral the lower side facing the yolk sac [f4]. The left–right axis is set during gastrulation and always means the embryo's own left and right [f5].

facts.text: The head–tail and back–belly axes are already set before the primitive streak appears.
The primitive streak first shows in the caudal midline of the disc; its cranial end is the primitive node.
The streak marks the long axis: it lies at the caudal (tail) end, and the cranial (head) end is opposite it.
Dorsal is the epiblast side, facing the amniotic cavity; ventral is the hypoblast side, facing the yolk sac.
Left and right are set during gastrulation; they are the embryo's own left and right sides.

misconceptions.wrong: Left and right mean the viewer's left and right.
misconceptions.right: They are the embryo's own sides, whichever way you look at it.

misconceptions.wrong: The groove (primitive streak) forms at the head end.
misconceptions.right: It forms in the caudal midline; the head end is opposite it.

checks.prompt: On the week-3 disc, where is the head (cranial) end?
options: Opposite the groove that forms at the tail end
On the underside, facing the yolk sac
It is not set until week 4
checks.why: The streak forms caudally, so the cranial end is the opposite end; the axis is set even before the streak.

checks.prompt: You face an embryo the way you face a person. Its left side is on…
options: Either side; left and right are not fixed
checks.why: Left and right are the embryo's own sides, so when you face it, its left is on your right.

checks.prompt: Which side of the disc is dorsal (the back)?
options: The upper side, facing the amniotic cavity
The lower side, facing the yolk sac
checks.why: Dorsal is the epiblast side, which faces the amniotic cavity; ventral faces the yolk sac.

adult: These three axes become the body's own head-to-toe, back-to-front and left–right directions [f1,f5].

remember.q: Which way does the long axis of the disc run?
remember.a: Head (cranial) to tail (caudal); the streak marks the tail end [f3].

remember.q: Which side of the disc is dorsal?
remember.a: The upper (epiblast) side, facing the amniotic cavity [f4].
